A further choice concerns how a model produces one vector for the whole paper. BERT, SciBERT, BioBERT and PubMedBERT produce an output vector at each token position, but were not trained specifically to compare whole documents. \subsection{Following the map from areas to individual papers}
A vector can be pictured as an arrow from a common starting point to the paper's position. Before comparison, I scale every arrow to length one, keeping the direction in which it points. To summarise an area, I average its article vectors and also scale the resulting vector to length one. I call this summary its \emph{centre}. before.en:
\subsection{Measuring shared structure and spread within an area}
To compare overall structure, I ask whether the same papers have similar patterns of relationships in two representations. The main measure is corrected linear centred kernel alignment, abbreviated CKA \citep{pmlr-v97-kornblith19a,refa961d84a4e}. A value near one, such as 0.9, indicates strong similarity between these patterns on this measure: the models organise the same objects in similar ways. It is an agreement score, not a percentage of correctly represented science. The correction reduces a known inflation caused by finite samples; it does not remove all statistical bias. Two further checks allow a rotation and rescaling of the representations (Procrustes alignment), or compare the ranking of distances between papers. They respond to different aspects of the representations \citep{NEURIPS2021_252a3dba,pmlr-v285-williams24a}. Supplement S2 gives the formulas.
before.es:
\subsection{Cómo se mide la estructura compartida y la dispersión de un área}
Para comparar la estructura general, examino si los mismos artículos mantienen un patrón parecido de relaciones en dos representaciones. La medida principal es la alineación lineal de núcleos centrados con corrección, abreviada CKA \citep{pmlr-v97-kornblith19a,refa961d84a4e}. Un valor cercano a uno, como 0,9, indica que esos patrones se parecen mucho según esta medida: los modelos organizan los mismos objetos de forma parecida. Es una puntuación de acuerdo, no un porcentaje de ciencia representada correctamente. La corrección reduce una inflación conocida debida al tamaño finito de la muestra; no elimina todo el sesgo estadístico. Otras dos comprobaciones permiten girar y cambiar de escala las representaciones para compararlas, mediante la alineación de Procrustes, o comparan el orden de las distancias entre artículos. Responden a aspectos distintos de las representaciones \citep{NEURIPS2021_252a3dba,pmlr-v285-williams24a}. El Suplemento S2 contiene las fórmulas.

before.en: I also describe two properties within each area. \emph{Angular spread} measures how far apart article vectors point: it summarises the angles between distinct vectors, using the median-distance convention in Supplement S6. Larger angles mean a wider spread of directions. \emph{Effective linear dimension}, measured by the participation ratio (PR), asks how widely variation is shared among directions. For intuition, a cloud concentrated along one line varies mainly in one direction; a cloud spread across a plane varies in more. The measure extends that idea to the full vector space. Neither property counts research topics or establishes how diverse an area is.

Para entenderlo, una nube concentrada a lo largo de una línea varía sobre todo en una dirección; una nube extendida sobre un plano varía en más. La medida lleva esta idea al espacio completo de los vectores. Ninguna de las dos propiedades cuenta temas de investigación ni establece lo diversa que es un área.
